propositions: fsck must detect and classify three dirty-tracker wedge classes: (1) tracked deletions of store artifacts restorable from HEAD, (2) untracked regenerable compaction leftovers, (3) orphaned .tmp-event-* files; each class is reported as a distinct finding with count and paths in both text and JSON output

doctor --repair must heal dirty-tracker wedges non-destructively using two sequential lock windows: window 1 (scoped write_lock) restores deletions via git checkout and quarantines leftovers without deletion; window 2 (released lock) invokes sync.reconverge which self-acquires the write lock to converge the store

Before any mutating repair action, doctor must record a backup ref at refs/rebar-doctor/<utc-ts> pointing to HEAD to provide an audit envelope; no backup ref means all mutating findings are unrepairable and repair exits with failure
fsck --output json must carry per-class counts and paths for tracker-dirty findings through registered _STRUCTURED_KINDS; paths are shlex-quoted for lossless text-to-JSON round-trip

The file-mutating repair window must respect existing lock semantics (a held write lock causes wait/fail per contract, not unlocked mutation) and must not delete files—only restore or move to quarantine
doctor --repair must be idempotent: running it on a clean store makes zero changes, creates no commits, and produces no backup ref
